text:
sam: Noticed tail latency climb on prod starting ~14:50 UTC. p50 unchanged, p95 +35ms, p99 +210ms, overall throughput down ~11%. Correlated with churn in kernel selection logs.

anya: which deployment/pool? any noisy-host alerts?

sam: Mostly on reserve-pool-2 and some spillovers to pool-4. Alerts showed increased admission queue and dispatch wait. Dumping the scheduler snapshot: 

sam: ```
Pool: reserve-pool-2
queue_length: 276
inflight_microbatches: 9
avg_microbatch_size: 1.4
avg_dispatch_wait_ms: 6.7
admission_rps: 82
```

rui: avg_microbatch_size of 1.4 is suspicious for this class of requests. We expect ~3.2 with current batching. Any recent changes to the batching window or admission logic?

sam: No batching config change. We did push a change to the kernel selector yesterday that prefers the new fused-qk kernel for q4 models when seq >=120.

kevin: I flagged that selector change as potentially regressive for tiny microbatches. The fused path reduces kernel launches but also reduces overlap with async copies for small sizes, so it can increase stalls.

anya: Do we have GPU-side traces or nvprof snippets from an affected host?

sam: Short extracted perf summary from node-gpu-12: 

sam: ```
GPU_profile:
  kernel_launches: 2188
  avg_kernel_ms: 0.52
  memcpy_h2d_block_ms: 0.14
  memcpy_d2h_block_ms: 0.09
  gpu_idle_pct: 20.1
  kv_cache_miss_pct: 19.7
  context_switch_ms: 1.5
```

rui: KV miss rate spiked as well. We rolled the kv eviction policy tweak last week to free space for packed entries—could be related.

kevin: Hypothesis: fused kernel increases working set per request (extra temporary tensors). Combined with more aggressive KV eviction, we evict prefixes more often -> more KV refills and DMA activity -> less overlapped work -> GPU idle spikes and higher tail latency.

clare: That sounds like a two-change interaction rather than a single root cause. We should do a canary rollback of the eviction change and/or change kernel selection heuristics for small batches.

anya: Quick mitigation options: bump min_batch_wait for affected pools (force slightly larger microbatches), apply a selector override to prefer legacy kernel if expected batch < 2.5, revert kv eviction tweak on a canary set. Which do we want to try first?

sam: I'll test bumping admission window on a few canary shards. Setting admission.min_wait_ms=14 for reserve-pool-2 canary shards in 5m. Command: 

sam: ```
/infra/deploys/pool-config set reserve-pool-2 admission.min_wait_ms=14 --canary
```

perf-bot: Canary deploy queued: reserve-pool-2 (2/10 shards)

20m later...

sam: Canary A results: avg_microbatch_size rose to 2.8, p99 reduced by ~130ms, throughput up ~6%. GPU idle down some but still above baseline (~7%).

kevin: That's promising. I'll prepare a selector patch that prefers legacy-unfused kernel when predicted batch_size < 2.5. That should avoid the async-copy overlap regression without relying on admission delay.

rui: Meanwhile I'm going to roll back the eviction threshold on the canary nodes to see KV miss impact. Revert should drop miss rate.

sam: Revert command applied to canary nodes. Perf snapshot after revert: kv_cache_miss_pct -> 3.5%, gpu_idle_pct -> 3.8%, p99 nearly baseline on canary.

anya: So both fixes help: admission bump buys time, selector fix removes the microbatch-size sensitivity, kv revert fixes cache churn. Proposed immediate plan: 
 - Promote KV eviction revert cluster-wide (canary validated)
 - Merge and rollout kernel-selector guard (prefer unfused for small batches)
 - Keep admission.min_wait_ms bump as temporary safety toggle for reserve pools (can reduce later)
 - Add perf alert for gpu_idle_pct > 10% and avg_microbatch_size < 2.0 for early detection

clare: I'll add an integration test that simulates high RPS low-latency requests with microbatch targets around 1-2 so future selectors are covered. Also adding a perf regression check on gpu_idle_pct and kv miss rates to CI.

kevin: PR for selector guard drafted, includes unit tests and a microbatch-sim harness. ETA 3h.

rui: KV eviction revert PR ready for review, will include histograms showing before/after cache hit curves. ETA 1h.

sam: Rolling promote of KV revert now to all reserve pools, keeping the admission bump in place until selector patch is rolled.

perf-bot: rollout status: KV eviction revert applied to 20/20 reserve-pool shards. Metrics trending to baseline.

sam: Nice. Leaving thread open for rollout monitoring and post-incident write-up. Initial diagnosis: interaction between new fused kernel and more aggressive KV eviction raised working set and broke copy/compute overlap for tiny microbatches -> increased GPU idle and tail latency. Root cause is cross-layer change coupling; mitigation path: selector heuristic, KV eviction tuning, and short-term batching delay.
